Hi Ava — thanks for the clear list. High-level responses below; attaching a concise PDF with clause suggestions (redwood_privdep_escrow_proposal.pdf).

1) Escrow release conditions
- Redwood will retain escrowed key material in a sealed HSM-managed vault. Release only on documented customer request AND a joint attestation process (customer-signed release form + notarized legal request for subpoenas/escrow release for business continuity).
- We will not release keys to any third party without the above.

2) Operator access and emergency maintenance
- Default posture: no Redwood operator has access to customer plaintext or model parameters in private deployments when BYOK is enabled.
- Breakglass: in exceptional emergency (safety incident, customer-approved incident response), operators may be granted JIT (just-in-time) access scoped to a single maintenance session. Controls:
  * Customer must provide one of the approved authorizers (pre-registered SSO identity) OR submit an authenticated breakglass request.
  * Access window: operator sessions are time-limited (suggested default 1 hour) and require multi-party approval (two internal approvers + customer authorization where practical).
  * All sessions are recorded, contain full command logs, and produce immutable audit bundles delivered to the customer (signed logs).
  * All operator actions are read-only where possible; modification requires explicit escalation and an auditable ticket.

3) Subprocessors and telemetry
- For private deployments we minimize external subprocessors. Typical subprocessors that may see metadata/telemetry: managed HSM provider (for escrow holding), cloud storage for immutable audit bundles (customer-chosen where possible), and our limited telemetry pipeline (anonymized usage metrics). Full subprocessor list and roles attached in the PDF.

4) Cross-border movement
- Default: control plane endpoints and audit bundles will be kept in the same region as the deployment. We will not route keystore material cross-border except with explicit customer approval and documented export controls.

Next steps
- I've asked Mateo to confirm the technical feasibility and wording for the operator session/recording artifacts. Irene will help translate this into DPA clause language and a short redline.

Regards,
Naomi Feldman
Sr. Counsel, Privacy & Contracts
Redwood Inference

Ava / Naomi / Irene — quick technical clarifications from infra side.

- HSM vs KMS: for escrow we use an HSM-backed vault. Escrow material stored in HSM and wrapped by customer CMK. Redwood engineers do not hold unwrap keys.
- Operator sessions: 1 hour default is reasonable, but for some maintenance tasks we may need a short extension (max 2 hours) with an automatic re-approval step in the system. We can implement a JIT workflow that:
  * Requires two internal approvers (SRE lead + Infra on-call)
  * Posts a signed, append-only log to a customer-designated S3/GCS bucket or to a customer-managed syslog stream
  * Produces a tamper-evident bundle (hash + signature) for packet of logs and artifacts that we push to the customer for retention.
- We can guarantee operator actions are isolated in a privileged container with no external network egress other than the signed artifact upload.

Attachment: BYOK-operator-matrix.pdf (matrix of operator roles, minimal-required permissions, and session artifacts).

Let us know if MediCore wants the operator log delivery to a customer-managed bucket (we recommend that for maximum control).

Thanks,
Mateo Alvarez
Staff Infra Engineer
Redwood Inference

Naomi / Mateo — thanks for the rapid detail, this is helpful. A few follow-ups from legal: 

- Escrow release: MediCore will accept the notarized release approach but requests explicit language that escrow release requires either: (a) customer-signed release OR (b) court order signed by a US federal or state judge; Redwood would be allowed to release to authorities only on receipt of that court order.
- Operator access window: we prefer a minimum notice of 4 hours for any non-emergency sessions; for true emergencies (safety/security), the 1-hour JIT model with joint approval is acceptable.
- Audit bundles: confirm retention period options (we ask for 7 years by default for health customers). Any storage costs?

I attached our redlines for the DPA as a starting point (MediCore_DPA_redlines_v2.docx). Can Redwood confirm: (1) no cross-border routing; (2) subprocessor list for HSM provider and audit storage; (3) whether Redwood will agree to notify MediCore 30 days before adding any new subprocessor that would touch escrow/audit artifacts?

Ava — thanks, and appreciate the redlines. Summary of commitments we can include in the revised DPA:

- Escrow release: Redwood will only release escrow material upon customer-signed release OR a valid court order. We will add explicit language to the DPA.
- Operator sessions: we will add 2-mode language: 4-hour notice for planned maintenance; 1-hour JIT model for emergencies with multi-approver workflow and recorded sessions; we will also include extension/reauthorization rules.
- Audit bundles: we can offer retention tiers; the default for healthcare customers will be 7 years. Storage costs will be billed as an add-on (we will quantify and show expected ranges).
- Subprocessor notification: Redwood will provide 30-days notice before adding any subprocessor that can access escrow/audit artifacts and will provide a mechanism for MediCore to review (and in exceptional cases request mitigations).

Next steps: Irene will produce a DPA redline incorporating the items above. I’ll schedule a 30-minute follow-up call with MediCore legal + infra for Thursday (proposed 11:00 AM ET) to walk the redlines and confirm delivery preferences for audit bundles.
